It contains application/example migrations referencing `auth.users`, but no matching core auth migration defining the tables or the described RLS-column change. The closest relevant Supabase documentation is:
  - [supabase:apps/docs/content/guides/auth/sessions.mdx?L30-L31](/r/github.com/sg-evals/supabase--v0.24.03/-/blob/apps/docs/content/guides/auth/sessions.mdx?L30-L31)

- PostgREST builds and stores a schema cache from PostgreSQL catalogs:
  - [postgrest:src/PostgREST/SchemaCache.hs?L78-L85](/r/github.com/sg-evals/postgrest--v12.0.2/-/blob/src/PostgREST/SchemaCache.hs?L78-L85) — cache contents.

  - [postgrest:src/PostgREST/SchemaCache.hs?L589-L657](/r/github.com/sg-evals/postgrest--v12.0.2/-/blob/src/PostgREST/SchemaCache.hs?L589-L657) — table/column discovery through `pg_attribute`, `pg_class`, and related catalogs.
  - [postgrest:src/PostgREST/SchemaCache.hs?L462-L482](/r/github.com/sg-evals/postgrest--v12.0.2/-/blob/src/PostgREST/SchemaCache.hs?L462-L482) — accessible-table privilege filtering.
  - [postgrest:src/PostgREST/AppState.hs?L306-L331](/r/github.com/sg-evals/postgrest--v12.0.2/-/blob/src/PostgREST/AppState.hs?L306-L331) — cache load, retry, and replacement behavior.
  - [postgrest:src/PostgREST/Query.hs?L173-L183](/r/github.com/sg-evals/postgrest--v12.0.2/-/blob/src/PostgREST/Query.hs?L173-L183) — OpenAPI/API exposure filtered using cached tables and current privileges.
  - [postgrest:src/PostgREST/Response/OpenAPI.hs?L43-L45](/r/github.com/sg-evals/postgrest--v12.0.2/-/blob/src/PostgREST/Response/OpenAPI.hs?L43-L45) — OpenAPI generation from cached metadata.

- No PostgREST `pg_policy`/RLS-policy introspection implementation was found in this snapshot. PostgREST generally delegates RLS evaluation to PostgreSQL during generated SQL execution; the schema cache holds table/column metadata and privileges, not a client-side policy evaluator. Therefore, a newly referenced policy column is not “resolved” by a separate PostgREST policy cache. A stale cache can omit the column from generated API metadata, while PostgreSQL itself evaluates the policy and may return permission errors if the effective role lacks access or the generated query conflicts with the changed schema.

- GoTrue’s session schema and hardcoded assumptions are explicit:

  - [gotrue:internal/models/refresh_token.go?L16-L35](/r/github.com/sg-evals/gotrue--v2.143.0/-/blob/internal/models/refresh_token.go?L16-L35) — hardcoded refresh-token columns including `session_id`, `revoked`, timestamps, and token-family fields.
  - [gotrue:internal/models/user.go?L19-L70](/r/github.com/sg-evals/gotrue--v2.143.0/-/blob/internal/models/user.go?L19-L70) — hardcoded `auth.users` model fields, including `id`, `aud`, `role`, `email`, password, confirmation/recovery fields, metadata, timestamps, and deletion/ban fields.
  - [gotrue:internal/models/user.go?L495-L551](/r/github.com/sg-evals/gotrue--v2.143.0/-/blob/internal/models/user.go?L495-L551) — refresh-token lookup loads the token, then user by `user_id`, then session by `session_id`.
  - [gotrue:internal/api/token_refresh.go?L23-L79](/r/github.com/sg-evals/gotrue--v2.143.0/-/blob/internal/api/token_refresh.go?L23-L79) and [L92-L230](/r/github.com/sg-evals/gotrue--v2.143.0/-/blob/internal/api/token_refresh.go?L92-L230) — refresh flow, session validity checks, locking, token rotation, session updates, and JWT generation.
  - [gotrue:internal/models/cleanup.go?L33-L72](/r/github.com/sg-evals/gotrue--v2.143.0/-/blob/internal/models/cleanup.go?L33-L72) — cleanup SQL assumes `sessions.refreshed_at`, `sessions.updated_at`, `refresh_tokens.session_id`, `refresh_tokens.revoked`, and `refresh_tokens.not_after`.

Likely impact chain:

1. A Supabase migration changes an auth table/policy column or session structure.
2. PostgREST’s catalog-derived cache remains stale until reload; generated table metadata/OpenAPI may omit new columns. PostgREST does not independently evaluate RLS policies—PostgreSQL does—so authenticated requests can receive database permission/RLS errors surfaced as HTTP authorization failures, commonly observed as 403s.
3. GoTrue’s ORM models and raw SQL assume the established session/user columns. Removing, renaming, changing types, or changing nullability of fields such as `session_id`, `refreshed_at`, `updated_at`, `aal`, `factor_id`, or `tag` can make refresh-token lookup, locking, validity checks, token rotation, and cleanup fail. Intermittency is especially consistent with concurrent refresh locking/retry behavior in `token_refresh.go`.
4. The new `auth.users` policy column itself should not break GoTrue merely by being additive if queries use `SELECT *` and the storage mapper tolerates extra columns; it becomes dangerous if RLS or grants cause GoTrue’s database role to lose access, or if the migration alters/removes columns GoTrue maps.
